https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/08/05/megk.text: Menü Kereső Megkezdődött a magyar nyelv és irodalom érettségi vizsgák átalakítása Belföld Bakró-Nagy Ferenc Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Megkezdődtek a magyar nyelv és irodalom érettségi vizsga korrekcióját előkészítő konzultációk – tudatta posztjában Lannert Judit. Az oktatási és gyermekügyi miniszter szerint az új Nemzeti alaptanterv előkészítésével párhuzamosan a közoktatás teljes tartalmi szabályozását is megújítják. A tárca tervei szerint az új, átmeneti szabályozás végleges formája ősszel kerülhet a nyilvánosság elé. „Miután az elmúlt években számos jogos szakmai kritika érte a jelenlegi magyar nyelv és irodalom érettségi vizsga szerkezetét és tartalmát – megkeserítve a középiskolás tanulók és tanáraik életét – ezért ennek a vizsgának az átalakítását már most megkezdtük. Első lépésként teljesen megújítottuk az érettségi tétel-előkészítő bizottságot. Az új szabályozásra vonatkozó javaslatot már az új bizottság készíti el” – írta. A cél egy sokkal átláthatóbb és igazságosabb magyar nyelv és irodalom érettségi, amely: csökkenti és egyértelművé teszi a középszintű követelményeket, pontosan megszabja az egyes feladattípusok sajátosságait, továbbá növeli a magyartanárok szakmai szabadságát . A tervek szerint nyár végén széles körű szakmai egyeztetés kezdődik a tervezetről, hogy a végleges szabályozás a pedagógusok és a szakmai szervezetek tapasztalataira is épüljön. „Ezzel végleg felszámoltuk azt a gyakorlatot, hogy egy politikai bizalmi tanácsadó egyszemélyben határozza meg egy ágazat jelenét és jövőjét, Takaró Mihály immár semmilyen befolyással nem bír az oktatás irányítására ” – közölte. Lannert Judit oktatási és gyermekügyi miniszter kinevezése után hamar belekezdett az oktatás átalakításának előkészítésébe. Szinte naponta ül le egyeztetni különböző szereplőkkel, jelent be változtatást, intézkedést a tanárok és a diákok életében, közben nyilatkozataiban a rendszerben lévő évtizedes problémákra mutat rá. Előre tudható volt, hogy az oktatáskutatóból lett miniszter egy olyan terület irányítását kapta meg, amiben kódolva vannak a konfliktusok. https://telex.hu/english/2026/08/21/elhu.text: Menü Kereső Hungary celebrates Statehood Day with colourful festivities English Photo: Lujza Hevesi-Szabó / Telex Ostyáni János Weiler Vilmos Andrea Horváth Kávai (translation) Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom A thousand-year-old country held a celebration dating back hundreds of years, with traditions stretching back centuries with a new government, a new prime minister, a new president, and a renewed public media. On Thursday, one half of Hungary woke up wondering how this year's St Stephen Day would differ from previous celebrations of August 20, while the other half woke up expecting the same traditions they had grown accustomed to. The latter group had it easy: the flag-raising ceremony, the swearing-in of military officers, the presentation of state awards, the procession with the Holy Right Hand of St Stephen and the flower carnival were all held just as they had been in previous years. And although the street vendors no longer offered beer at the heavily subsidised price of 350 forints as in the last few years of the Orbán regime, the Gripen jets still flew over Budapest, and the fireworks—which cost only a fraction of the previous years’ displays—were no less spectacular than before. President András Baka at the raising of Hungary’s flag on Kossuth Square in Budapest during the celebration of the founding of the state and St Stephen's Day, on August 20, 2026,. Behind him is Colonel General Zsolt Sándor, Chief of the General Staff of the Hungarian Armed Forces – Photo: Dániel István Alföldi / Telex Photo: Dániel István Alföldi / Telex Prime Minister Péter Magyar delivered a speech after the Minister of Defense addressed the troops – Photo: Dániel István Alföldi / Telex After the raising of the flag and the commissioning ceremony, three Gripen jets flew over Kossuth Square, marking the start of the air parade over the Danube – Photo: Dániel István Alföldi / Telex Photo: Péter Lakatos / MTI President András Baka, Prime Minister Péter Magyar, and Ágnes Forsthoffer, Speaker of the House presented state honors on the occasion of the holiday – Photo: Róbert Hegedüs / MTI The display of the Hungarian Postal Service at the 57th Debrecen Flower Carnival on 20 August – Photo: Zsolt Czeglédi / MTI A Lynx KF41 infantry combat vehicle at the display of military equipment by the Hungarian Defense Forces in Városliget – Photo: Péter Lakatos / MTI The most interesting political event of the day was the first national meeting of the Tisza Islands, attended by more than a thousand members of the Tisza Party's volunteers from across the country. As it turned out, most of them felt that since 12 April communication from the party leadership has become scarce, and that their role in the new situation remained unclear. Others, however, said that even in this “standby mode,” with things left to their own devices, they’ve managed to find their footing. The national gathering of the Tisza Party's volunteers was held on Margaret Island in a cordoned-off area of Nagyrét, with the press kept out – Photo: Lujza Hevesi-Szabó / Telex Visitors stand in line at Kossuth Square; visiting the Parliament Building was free to the public in honor of the holiday – Photo: Noémi Bruzák / MTI Fresh loaves of bread awaiting the judges at the Kenyérlelke Festival at the Open-Air Ethnographic Museum in Szentendre, which put on presentations featuring bakeries, mills, and farmers, as well as a craft fair for visitors – Photo: Zoltán Kocsis / MTI Handicrafts festival at Szentháromság Tér in Buda Castle – Photo: Zoltán Kocsis / MTI There was an open house at the former Carmelite Monastery, which housed the Prime Minister's offices in recent years. Now, anyone could check out the view from Viktor Orbán’s former office – Photo: Lajos Soós / MTI The Holy Right Hand of St Stephen was carried around during the procession held on the anniversary of the founding of the state and in honor of King Saint Stephen on October 6 Street – Photo: Zoltán Máthé / MTI One of the big questions ahead of the festivities was whether the celebratory program and the Budapest fireworks display traditionally closing it out would go off without a hitch. The previous government had contracted Gyula Balásy’s companies -known for providing overpriced services for state events (enriching Balásy overnight)- for putting the event on. After the government change, a new organizer was brought in, who only had a few weeks and a much smaller budget than originally planned for organizing the show. In the end, the result did not disappoint. Photo: Lujza Hevesi-Szabó, Dániel István Alföldi / Telex Photo: Zoltán Balogh / MTI There were three different locations for those looking to party before and after the fireworks in the capital; one of them, Kossuth Square was completely packed—Photo: Lujza Hevesi-Szabó / Telex Photo: Lujza Hevesi-Szabó / Telex

https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world.text: Volodymyr Zelensky has warned airlines that Russia’s airspace will is “completely unsafe” ahead of Ukrainian drone strikes. The Ukrainian president issued the warning in his nightly video address, saying he did not want innocent lives to be lost, but “the safe days in Russia’s skies are over.” “Today, we want to warn every airline that uses Russian airspace, every insurer, and everyone who still uses Russia’s key airports: Russian airspace is becoming completely unsafe. “Ukraine does not threaten civilian aviation as such – not a single civilian aircraft. There will simply be drones in Russia’s skies on a scale that has to be taken into account. “Although the Russian authorities are not properly informing people about this, Russian airspace will effectively be closing – the war started by Russia is closing its skies. “It is important that this is heard by the ambassadors of countries represented here in Ukraine, as well as by ambassadors working in Moscow. “It is important that the airlines currently flying to airports primarily in Moscow, St. Petersburg, and other key destinations in Russia hear this as well.”

Beállítom Több alkalommal is a Tiborcz István érdekeltségébe tartozó Dorothea Hotelben szállásolták el a Külgazdasági és Külügyminisztérium vendégeit Szijjártó Péter minisztersége alatt, számolt be az RTL Híradó. Az RTL információi szerint ezeket a minisztérium fizette. A Budapest belvárosában található hotel a Tiborcz István-féle BDPST-csoporthoz tartozik. A Dorothea Hotel 2024 tavaszán nyílt meg, az RTL információi szerint három hónappal később már fogadta is a külügy vendégeit. A hotel első külügyes vendége Oroszország egészségügyi minisztere, Mihail Murasko volt, aki 2024 szeptemberében tárgyalt Szijjártó Péterrel Budapesten. Ezután Afrika egyik legkisebb államának vezetője, Bissau-Guinea korábbi elnöke is a Dorotheában kapott szállást, de itt szállt meg a kolumbiai elnök és felesége, valamint a türk államok szervezetének főtitkára is. Utóbbi elszállásolása több mint 15 millió forintba került. 2026-ban a cseh miniszterelnöknek, Andrej Babišnak is itt foglaltak szobát, aki a jobboldali konferenciára, a CPAC Hungaryre érkezett volna Budapestre. Az RTL szerint Babiš szállását is a Külgazdasági és Külügyminisztérium fedezte volna, pedig a rendezvényt nem a minisztérium, hanem a kormányközeli Alapjogokért Központ szervezte. Babiš végül egy csehországi raktártűz miatt nem vett részt a konferencián. A Dorothea volt az a hotel, ahol az Orbán Ráhel-féle influenszertrip résztvevőinek egy része is megszállt. Nemrég derült ki, hogy a Budapest Influencer Trip projekt teljes költsége nettó 3,1809 milliárd forint volt. A hotel épületében üzemel többek között Orbán Ráhel bababoltja, az Odu Store is. Az utazások költségeiről kérdéseket küldtünk a Külügyminisztériumnak, amennyiben érdemben válaszolnak, frissíteni fogjuk a cikket. UK news Leader of group behind flag campaign in England charged with 14 offences Ryan Bridge, who co-founded Raise the Colours, to appear in court on charges including racially aggravated harassment Neha Gohil Midlands correspondent Mon 7 Sep 2026 06.43 EDT Last modified on Mon 7 Sep 2026 07.04 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The leader of a group responsible for raising union jack and St George’s flags across England has been charged with 14 offences, including racially aggravated harassment, threatening behaviour and assault. Ryan Bridge, 45, of Bromsgrove, Worcestershire, co-founded Raise the Colours, which describes itself as a “grassroots movement for unity and patriotism”. The group’s members have been erecting union jack and St George’s flags on roundabouts, lampposts and other street furniture across England since August last year. Thames Valley police said they had charged Bridge with 14 offences from a two-month period in Oxfordshire from 31 January 2026. He is due to appear at Oxford magistrates court on 3 November. The offences are: Seven counts of using threatening words or behaviour to cause harassment, alarm or distress. Three counts of using threatening, abusive or insulting words or behaviour with intent to cause fear of, or provoke, unlawful violence. Two counts of racially aggravated intentional harassment, alarm or distress. One count of racially aggravated fear of violence. One count of common assault. Officers said a file was prepared and submitted to the Crown Prosecution Service after a review of the evidence, including witness accounts and available footage. Oxfordshire county council was granted an injunction against Bridge and others to prevent anyone from raising flags on public property, citing safety concerns as well as trespass and obstruction. Birmingham city council announced last week it was seeking a similar injunction against Bridge and others. The application will be heard at the high court on Tuesday. Bridge attended the Reform UK conference in Birmingham at the weekend, and told the Guardian he was invited by the party. “We got an invite, so we thought we would come along,” he said. There were no general admission tickets to the Reform conference for members of the public, where attenders were almost entirely members. Farage praised Bridge and his group’s efforts at a conference event on Saturday, telling him: “What your campaign has done is wake up vast parts of this country.” At the time, Bridge was on bail after he was arrested by Thames Valley police on suspicion of causing racially and religiously aggravated harassment, alarm or distress earlier this year. Bridge has previously denied any wrongdoing. The Pivnichnyi (Northern) Bridge, has been hit for the second day in a row, while the Pivdennyi (Southern) Bridge was hit multiple times earlier this week. The latest attack came as German Chancellor Friedrich Merz made a visit to Kyiv on Sunday. BBC Ukraine correspondent Dan Johnson is near one of the bridges that was targeted and explains what we know so far.
